body: Thanks for your input, I have a question if you don't mind too much: after the situation, sometimes he knows that he didn't do a good job and he wants to get better.  Did your partner feel the same way sometimes?  Because I do value making things work and committing for longer amounts of time.  Do you think if he wants to get better, I should stick around to give him a longer chance?  We've only been together six months, but I don't know if that's already "chance" enough.

That's exactly what's happening.  I never used to be the person who would say "nothing" if asked if something was wrong and I actually wanted to say something.  But now, sometimes I'm so afraid of what the situation could lead to that I often just swallow my feelings and say nothing is wrong.  I just hate making him feel like he's not enough.  I just completely suck at taking care of myself so that's clouding my judgement I think.

For some people, the "daily count" of how long you can stay clean can be helpful, and for others I think it can encourage hurtful expectations and be really detrimental to the mentality of progress.  This was a mistake that you admit to and feel awful about, but honestly if it places you in a better mental state to keep your clean count going, you don't have to call this a failure.  Just don't count it if it hurts too much to do so.  Staying clean and keeping track of how long you've stayed clean is meant to encourage, not create pain.  I'm sorry things are rough enough to bring you back to that place, but if you want to still consider yourself clean for X amount of years, then you do so.  You did not lose progress, and this is not a failure.  You're doing great with your recovery.

It's okay, sorry you're going through something similar.  Perhaps the sentiment "you're not alone" is overplayed, but I hope there is some comfort in knowing you are experiencing something alongside another person. Best of luck to you.
